stories.title: Arizona Tradeport Hubs Receives $16M Federal Grant
stories.excerpt: The plan is to streamline cargo movement and transform domestic supply chains across the country, initially stretching from California to Arizona and all the way to the East Coast. The so-called tradeport hubs project, which will be rolled out in multiple phases, intends to integrate a web of highways, train tracks and airlines within manufacturing hot spots across the U.S. The Phoenix Business Journal reports that the latest $16 million infusion of government funds will go toward developing the first three tradeport hubs, each ranging from 1,000 to 5,000 acres along the I-40 corridor. The first route is planned to connect the Port of Los Angeles to Albuquerque, New Mexico and to the BNSF Southern Transcon Railroad through northern Arizona. The two key tradeport hubs identified in Arizona are in Kingman and Winslow. An initial estimate of the total development costs for the hub in Winslow is pegged at $750 million. Global Logistics Development Partners is spearheading the effort in Arizona. The post Arizona Tradeport Hubs Receives $16M Federal Grant appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Federal grant of $16M awarded for Arizona tradeport hubs along I-40 corridor in Kingman, Winslow
Winslow hub estimated at $750M total development cost; 1,000–5,000 acres per hub
Infrastructure project connects Port of Los Angeles to Albuquerque and BNSF rail network
stories.summary: The federal government is funding the first phase of a multiphase tradeport hub project spanning from California to the East Coast. Arizona's two key hubs—Kingman and Winslow—received $16 million in initial funding as part of a larger effort to integrate highways, rail, and air cargo networks. The Winslow hub alone is projected to cost $750 million.
stories.impact: Logistics infrastructure expansion in northern Arizona signals anticipated industrial and commercial growth along the I-40 corridor, which could drive employment and population inflow to Kingman, Winslow, and surrounding areas within 5–10 years. Multifamily developers should monitor industrial employment clusters and supply-chain job creation in these markets for future rental demand uplift; however, timing and scale remain uncertain pending additional federal funding approvals.

stories.title: OHT Breaks Ground on 360-Unit Houston Rental Community
stories.excerpt: OHT Partners has begun construction of a 360-unit apartment complex called Park Row at 14192 Park Row Blvd. in Houston. OHT recently broke ground on another project, 5 miles to the west on Park Row Boulevard. Dubbed Park Row, it will have 11 three-story buildings, a clubhouse, a pet spa and a bike storage facility on 13.7 acres. The one- and two-bedroom units will range from 702 to 1,257 square feet. Community amenities include a fitness room, coworking areas with private offices, a kitchen, package lockers, a resort-style pool with cabanas, a dog park and wash, a pickleball court, detached garages, electric vehicle chargers and outdoor grills. Meeks + Partners is the architect for the project, and OHT serves as its own general contractor. OHT anticipates starting pre-leasing in the second quarter of next year and complete the complex in the second quarter of 2028. The rental rate will be determined around the time pre-leasing begins. The company acquired the property last February. bullets: OHT Partners breaks ground on Park Row: 360-unit apartment complex in Houston on 13.7 acres

stories.summary: OHT Partners has begun construction on Park Row, a 360-unit rental community in Houston featuring one- and two-bedroom units between 702 and 1,257 square feet. The project, spread across 13.7 acres in 11 three-story buildings, includes high-end amenities such as a resort-style pool, coworking spaces, and EV charging. Pre-leasing is scheduled for Q2 2026 with completion targeted for Q2 2028.
stories.impact: Another 360-unit delivery entering Houston's supply pipeline in 2028 adds to an already robust multifamily construction cycle in the metro. Rental rates will be set at pre-leasing (Q2 2026); monitoring how the wider Houston market absorbs concurrent deliveries will signal whether this premium-amenity product commands rent growth sufficient to support development feasibility in 2026–2027 land acquisition windows.

stories.title: AvalonBay, Equity Residential Will Operate as Vivmark Post-Merger
stories.excerpt: AvalonBay Communities, Inc. and Equity Residential announced Vivmark Residential as the name for the combined company resulting from their merger of equals. The new company, which expects to trade under the ticker symbol VMRK, will have a pro forma equity market capitalization of approximately $53 billion and an enterprise value of approximately $71 billion, with more than 180,000 rental apartments and over 10,000 apartments under construction. “The name Vivmark Residential reflects what we are building — a company determined to set a new standard for the experience of home,” said Benjamin Schall, CEO of AvalonBay and incoming CEO of Vivmark..”Vivmark Residential is built from the exceptional foundations that AvalonBay and Equity Residential have each spent more than 30 years establishing as trusted leaders. With the combined scale, capabilities, and talent of both organizations, we have a rare opportunity to redefine what rental housing can be.” The combined company will operate as Vivmark Residential upon completion of the merger. The new company name will not result in community name changes at closing. It’s not yet clear where the combined company will be headquartered. Where the apartment industry connects. Build relationships, uncover opportunities, and stay ahead of what’s next. The post AvalonBay, Equity Residential Will Operate as Vivmark Post-Merger appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AvalonBay + Equity Residential merger creates Vivmark Residential: $53B equity cap, $71B enterprise value
Combined portfolio: 180,000+ rental apartments, 10,000+ units under construction; trades as VMRK
Benjamin Schall (AvalonBay CEO) becomes CEO of combined entity; headquarters location TBD
stories.summary: AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential have completed their merger of equals, forming Vivmark Residential with a pro forma equity market capitalization of $53 billion and enterprise value of $71 billion. The combined company will operate over 180,000 rental apartments with more than 10,000 units under construction and will trade on the NYSE under ticker VMRK. Benjamin Schall, former AvalonBay CEO, will lead the new entity; individual property names will not change at closing.
stories.impact: Creation of a $71B multifamily giant consolidates development capital, land platforms, and operating scale; watch for Vivmark to accelerate or redeploy development pipelines, divest non-core markets, and refinance debt at lower blended rates post-close. Competitors and land sellers should expect competitive pressure from Vivmark's scale on site acquisition and construction management costs in major metros, potentially reshaping development feasibility for smaller builders.

stories.title: DFW Airport Slated to Pay $193.6M for Hyatt Hotel
stories.excerpt: The DFW Airport already owns the Grand Hyatt DFW, Hyatt Place DFW and Hyatt House, which is under construction and slated to open in summer 2027. It’s now eyeing a fourth Hyatt hotel property. DFW Airport’s Public Facility Improvement Corp. board recently approved the purchase of Hyatt Regency DFW International Airport, located next to Terminal C. That vote will trigger a few more votes before the transaction is finalized. Dallas and Fort Worth have to give the deal its final approval. Under the agreement, the airport would buy the hotel and its leasehold interest for up to $193.65 million while Hyatt continues to manage the property. Woodbine and Castle Lake bought the hotel in 2021. The bid for Hyatt Regency also comes as the airport recently opened the first phase of an expanded Terminal C, which included five rebuilt gates and four new ones exclusively for American Airlines Group Inc. bullets: DFW Airport approves $193.6M purchase of Hyatt Regency DFW near Terminal C; Hyatt to manage

stories.summary: DFW Airport's board approved the purchase of Hyatt Regency DFW International Airport for up to $193.65 million, adjacent to Terminal C. The airport will own the hotel while Hyatt continues management. This acquisition follows recent expansions of Terminal C with nine gates added exclusively for American Airlines, and follows ongoing construction of a Hyatt House property slated to open summer 2027.
stories.impact: Airport investment in hospitality infrastructure and terminal expansion signals confidence in DFW traffic and business travel recovery. Sustained airport modernization and American Airlines gateway expansion support both business-travel demand and corporate relocation to the Dallas–Fort Worth metro, benefiting multifamily rental demand. Monitor job creation announcements among airline, logistics, and tech firms in DFW over next 12–18 months to identify demand tailwinds for apartment developers.

stories.title: Schuckman Realty Buys Northeast Queens Shopping Center for $56M
stories.excerpt: Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center in Queens for $56 million. Long Island-based Schuckman Realty purchased the Key Food-anchored property at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway, according to a deed transfer in property records filed Friday. The purchase could be a play for assets tied to grocery stores and other necessity-based retail. Acadia Realty Trust provided about $48.5 million in financing to Schuckman for the acquisition through a shell corporation, with Acadia’s Chief Financial Officer John Gottfried signing the mortgage documents. Schuckman, Punia & Marx and Acadia did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Punia & Marx has owned the property since at least 1975, and the amount paid for that acquisition is unknown. Schuckman seems to have been involved in the management operations of the 220,000-square-foot shopping center, which is also leased to a Chase Bank branch, with a 2020 flier listing Kenneth Schuckman and Jessica Vilmenay as exclusive brokers. The advertisement said at the time that a redevelopment of the property would be taking place, but was not specific about the nature of the repositioning. Schuckman promoted the center based on 100,000 cars passing by the center daily on the Cross Island Parkway and 333,000 people living within three miles. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Schuckman Realty buys Whitestone Shopping Center (Queens) for $56M; Key Food anchor, 220,000 sq ft
Acadia Realty Trust provided $48.5M financing via shell corp; Punia & Marx sold after 50+ years
Property at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway also leases to Chase Bank; necessity-based retail focus
stories.summary: Long Island-based Schuckman Realty purchased the Whitestone Shopping Center in Queens for $56 million from Punia & Marx Real Estate, which had owned it since at least 1975. The 220,000-square-foot Key Food-anchored property at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway also houses a Chase Bank branch. Acadia Realty Trust provided approximately $48.5 million in HUD-backed debt financing for the acquisition.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Retail transaction signals investor confidence in necessity-based anchors in outer-borough Queens, but does not indicate residential demand shifts. Monitor if this acquisition leads to mixed-use redevelopment or zoning changes that could unlock multifamily density on or near the site in future.

stories.title: Dwight Capital Provides $24M Refi on New Jersey Multifamily Building
stories.excerpt: New Jersey developer Fadi Samaan has landed $23.5 million of U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)-backed debt to refinance a multifamily complex in Passaic, NJ., Commercial Observer has learned. Dwight Capital supplied the HUD 223(f) loan on the 104-unit Station at Passaic Phase II development, completed in 2024. The deal, which was originated by Dwight Capital’s Jonathan Pomper and Noah Greenwald, closed nearly a year to the date of a $27.7 million HUD 223(f) loan the private lender executed for the adjacent 104-unit Station at Passaic Phase I property in August 2025. Loan proceeds will be used to retire existing debt, establish a replacement reserve account for funding future capital improvements and return equity built up during the construction and lease-up stages, according to Dwight. “Station at Passaic’s location on the NJ Transit line into Manhattan drives strong renter demand from both New York City and other New Jersey submarkets,” Pomper said in a statement. “With tight vacancy, limited new supply, and neighborhood amenities like the on-site restaurant and grocery store, the property is well positioned to meet that demand as reflected in Phase I’s strong lease-up and the natural progression to Phase II.” Located at 99 Passaic Street 14 miles west of Midtown Manhattan, Station at Passaic Phase II consists of two five-story apartment buildings with a unit mix of eight one-bedroom and 96 two-bedroom units. The property also features 7,813 square feet of retail space that includes a Pachos Mini Market. Samaan said in a statement that the loan closing process with Dwight was “even smoother than the last” and credited them with “making even the most complex financing feel straightforward.” Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Dwight Capital funds $23.5M HUD 223(f) refi on Station at Passaic Phase II (104 units, completed 2024)
Phase I adjacent property received $27.7M HUD loan in Aug 2025; combined ~208 units on NJ Transit line
Loan proceeds retire debt, fund reserves, return equity from construction/lease-up stages
stories.summary: New Jersey developer Fadi Samaan secured a $23.5 million HUD 223(f) loan from Dwight Capital to refinance the 104-unit Station at Passaic Phase II, completed in 2024. The adjacent Phase I property (also 104 units) received a $27.7 million HUD loan in August 2025. Both projects benefit from proximity to the NJ Transit rail line serving Manhattan, driving demand from NYC and NJ submarkets.
stories.impact: Successful refi of recently completed Phase II signals strong lease-up absorption and operator confidence in the NJ Transit corridor as a rental demand engine. Passaic's connectivity to Manhattan via rail is attracting multifamily capital and demonstrating that secondary-market NJ locations with direct NYC transit access support both development feasibility and competitive refinancing. Developers should prioritize NJ Transit–adjacent land acquisition in Passaic, Newark, and Jersey City submarkets ahead of broader mid-market transit-oriented development.

stories.title: Prominent Austin Office Tower Trades for $208M
stories.excerpt: Cousins Properties Inc. has sold the One Eleven Congress office building in downtown Austin to Canyon Creek Real Estate. Cousins sold the One Eleven Congress office building for $208 million. Eastdil Secured brokered the sale. The Austin Business Journal reports building improvements may include modernizing common areas and possibly adding a tenant lounge. Other big transactions in Austin of late include Cousins’ purchase of the Sail Tower for $522 million in 2024, a deal that Eastdil served as exclusive adviser, and Brandywine’s sale of 405 Colorado to Hines earlier this month, another deal that involved Eastdil as Brandywine’s representative. Built in 1987, One Eleven Congress is part of the Central Business District’s older office buildings. At 503,344 square feet, the 30-story building is the seventh-largest office tower in Austin. As of June 2025, One Eleven Congress was 84% leased. The property is Canyon Creek’s first in Austin. The Fort Worth-based firm was formed in 2025. bullets: Canyon Creek Real Estate acquires One Eleven Congress (Austin office tower) from Cousins Properties for $208M

The 503,344-square-foot, 30-story building was completed in 1987 and was 84% leased as of June 2025. Canyon Creek, a Fort Worth-based firm founded in 2025, intends to modernize common areas and possibly add a tenant lounge.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Office tower trade reflects steady investor appetite for older Class B office assets in Austin's CBD with upside through modernization, but does not signal residential demand or supply changes. Monitor if office conversion-to-residential projects emerge in downtown Austin's aging office stock as tech and corporate hiring slows.

stories.title: AvalonBay Communities, Equity Residential Merger Produces Vivmark Residential
stories.excerpt: A new company brings a new name. Two months after multifamily giants AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential merged to form one of the country’s largest real estate companies — the total enterprise value is calculated at $71 billion — the two firms announced Friday that their new company will be called Vivmark Residential. The new firm, which is a publicly traded real estate investment trust (REIT), will hold the New York Stock Exchange ticker symbol VMRK. “The name Vivmark Residential reflects what we are building — a company determined to set a new standard for the experience of home,” said Benjamin Schall, CEO of AvalonBay Communities and the new CEO of the combined entity. The new name combines two words — Viv, from the Latin word “vivere,” or “to live fully,” and the English word “mark,” meaning “quality, distinction, and lasting impact,” according to a release from AvalonBay. “Vivmark Residential is built from the exceptional foundations that AvalonBay and Equity Residential have each spent more than 30 years establishing as trusted leaders,” added Schall. Vivmark Residential will take control of the residential REIT landscape as the new biggest player on the block. The combined entity will hold a portfolio of more than 180,000 rental apartments across 600 distinct apartment communities and assets, with another 10,800 units and $4.4 billion of development in its construction pipeline. AvalonBay stock currently trades at $187 per share, as of Friday morning, down 2 percent over the last five days, while Equity Residential stock trades at $67 per share, also down 2 percent in the last week. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2026. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vivmark Residential formed from AvalonBay–Equity Residential merger: $71B enterprise value, 180,000+ apartments
VMRK ticker on NYSE; Benjamin Schall (AvalonBay) is new CEO; 10,000+ units under construction
Property names unchanged at close; headquarters location to be determined
stories.summary: AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential have completed their merger to form Vivmark Residential, a publicly traded REIT with enterprise value of $71 billion, equity market cap of $53 billion, and over 180,000 apartments in operation plus 10,000+ units under construction. The company will trade on the NYSE under ticker VMRK, led by Benjamin Schall as CEO. Individual community names will remain unchanged.
stories.impact: Duplicate of article #3; see impact there. This consolidation reshapes competitive dynamics for multifamily land, development, and construction management across all major U.S. metros.

stories.title: Tom Giordano of Suffolk Construction: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: From a young age, Tom Giordano, general manager of the New York region for Suffolk Construction, had one goal. That was to follow in his uncle’s footsteps and become a lawyer to benefit his community. After going from litigation to representing general contractors, developers and design professionals on legal matters, he joined Morse Diesel Construction in 1999, then Bovis Lend Lease in 2004 as general counsel. For the last four and a half years, he has been managing the New York office of Suffolk Construction, working in a non-legal executive role. Giordano is responsible for enhancing the company’s internal organization processes and its infrastructure, as well as ensuring Suffolk is in a strong position to grow and expand construction management projects in the metro area — which for the firm includes New York City, Westchester and Long Island — in the hospitality, health care and residential spaces. Commercial Observer caught up with Giordano in July to discuss what projects Suffolk has been working on recently, notable market trends in New York City’s construction industry, and how the firm takes a project from an idea to reality. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What is the mission of Suffolk Construction in New York? Tom Giordano: Our mission is pretty simple. We want New York to be similar to what Suffolk is nationally. We want to be not necessarily the biggest, but the best construction management firm in the New York metro area, and deliver the Suffolk culture here. We’ve had a New York presence for 13 years, but we’ve really gotten a significant amount of traction over the last five and a half years. We’ve grown significantly. When I started, we were probably doing $350 million a year in revenue. Now we’re doing $1.3 billion, with a real look at $2 billion a year in the next two years. stories.summary: Tom Giordano, general manager of Suffolk Construction's New York region, oversees operations across New York City, Westchester, and Long Island, managing hospitality, healthcare, and residential construction projects. Giordano has spent 4.5 years in this role after transitioning from legal roles at Morse Diesel and Bovis Lend Lease, focusing on internal process enhancement and market expansion in the tristate region.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs Group Deploys $116M for Syracuse Affordable Housing Overhaul
stories.excerpt: Goldman Sachs has provided a $116 million construction loan as part of an overall $269 million financing package to facilitate the redevelopment of a long-standing Syracuse affordable housing complex, Commercial Observer can first report. The investment bank’s Urban Investment Group provided the loan on BFC Partners and SAA Canopy Group’s transformation of the Parkside Commons Section 8-backed housing complex in Syracuse’s East Side neighborhood. The project will feature 393 apartments designated as affordable through a combination of newly constructed and renovated units. “Parkside Commons represents a significant investment in not only the preservation but also the creation of affordable housing in Syracuse,” Asahi Pompey, chair of the Urban Investment Group at Goldman Sachs, said in a statement. “We are proud to partner with New York State, BFC Partners, and SAA Canopy Group to deliver quality homes that will serve Syracuse families for years to come.” The $269 million financing package also includes federal and state Low-Income Housing Tax Credits slated to raise $88 million and $13.6 million, respectively. The remainder of the funds will derive from interest earnings on tax-exempt bond proceeds for the development and interim project income generated during construction, according to BFC. BFC and SAA acquired the 15-acre property on 1901 East Fayette Street in late 2024 from a partnership connected to developer Stephen Ross, the Syracuse Post-Standard reported at the time. The 10-building complex, constructed in the mid-20th century, had previously faced security and crime challenges, according to the Post-Standard. Loan proceeds will be used for BFC and SAA Canopy to renovate six of the current buildings at the complex and build two new ones, which will have enough space to relocate all current residents from the four oldest structures slated for demolition The site of the demolished buildings will later be used for additional housing in a later developm
bullets: Goldman Sachs Urban Investment Group deploys $116M construction loan for Syracuse Parkside Commons redevelopment
Total financing package: $269M; 393 apartments (new + renovated), Section 8 affordable housing preservation

stories.summary: Goldman Sachs' Urban Investment Group provided a $116 million construction loan as part of a $269 million total financing package for the redevelopment of Parkside Commons, a Section 8 affordable housing complex in Syracuse's East Side. The project, led by BFC Partners and SAA Canopy Group, will deliver 393 apartments through a combination of newly constructed and renovated units. Financing includes federal and state Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) support.
stories.impact: Capital flowing into secondary-market affordable housing preservation signals continued investor appetite for LIHTC and HUD-backed deals in smaller metros. Syracuse's Parkside project demonstrates feasibility of mixed preservation/new-construction models in weak rental markets, but limited upside on market-rate rental demand. Developers should track LIHTC allocation trends and state affordable housing programs in secondary cities for stabilized cash-flow opportunities, though demand growth for market-rate apartments in Syracuse remains subdued.
